To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we have built an automated system that can train classifiers to predict the actionability of alerts generated by static analysis tools; (b) we have trained and evaluated three different machine-learning classifiers to predict the future actionability of alerts, using the actionability of past alerts as training data; (c) we have shown that a classifier based on lifetime alone can predict the actionability with a high degree of accuracy, outperforming the more complex classifiers.
the lifetime of alerts can be used to classify alerts as actionable or non-actionable with high precision and recall.
the lifetime of a bug report is a good indicator for the likelihood of an alert being acted upon.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the usefulness of alerts generated by automated static analysis tools.
the question of whether it is possible to use historic alert data of a static analysis tool to improve its usefulness.
the following questions: (1) Can we build a classifier that is able to identify actionable alerts based on historic alert data?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
it depends on the project, the type of alerts, the alerting tool, and the classifier which one works best.
the use of machine learning to classify alerts is a promising approach to improve the usefulness of alerts generated by automated static analysis tools.
a classifier that uses the alert lifetime as the only feature is the most effective classifier for our sample of software projects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lifetime of an alerts is the most important factor for determining actionability.
the lifetime-based classifier is the best approach to improve the usefulness of alerts generated by automated static analysis tools, but it is not the only one.
we have built a framework to collect historic alerts, trained several classifiers to classify new alerts and evaluated the classifiers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
machine-learning classifiers can be used to improve the usefulness of static analysis alerts.
it is possible to train classifiers to predict the actionability of static analysis alerts.

it is indeed possible to use machine learning techniques to improve the usefulness of alerts generated by static analysis tools, and that the approach is general enough to be applied to different software projects.
